title: Remove Punctuation: how it works, formula and examples
excerpt: Remove Punctuation: Strip punctuation and symbols while preserving letters, numbers, line breaks and optional apostrophes. Learn how to use it, the formula…
content:
The [Remove Punctuation](/remove-punctuation) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Strip punctuation and symbols while preserving letters, numbers, line breaks and optional apostrophes. Enter your text and apostrophes and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

Removing punctuation can prepare text for keyword comparison, simple tokenisation, normalised searches or data-cleaning workflows. This tool preserves Unicode letters, numbers and whitespace while removing punctuation and symbol characters. You can retain straight or curly apostrophes for contractions and possessives, or remove them for a stricter letters-and-numbers-only result. This guide explains how to use it, the formula it applies, and a worked example you can follow with your own numbers.

## How to use the Remove Punctuation

Start by typing or pasting your text, then choosing your apostrophes from the list. The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause. When you want a clean slate, Reset restores the defaults.

1. Paste the text and choose whether apostrophes should survive.
2. Review the cleaned result before using it in a search index, comparison or downstream transformation.
3. Keep the original separately when punctuation carries meaning, such as in code, URLs, decimals or formal writing.

## Formula

Keep every character in Unicode letter, number or whitespace categories, plus apostrophes in keep mode. Remove all other punctuation and symbol characters without changing line structure.

That is the standard formula for this calculation, and it is the same one the [Remove Punctuation](/remove-punctuation) applies to the values you enter. You can work it out by hand, but the calculator is faster when you want to try several values, and it removes the risk of a slip in the arithmetic.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. With apostrophes kept, “Hello, world! It's 2026.” becomes “Hello world It's 2026”; the sentence punctuation is removed and the original spacing remains. Try the same figures in the [Remove Punctuation](/remove-punctuation) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves.

## What the result shows

With the default values (Text: Hello, world! It's a useful text-cleaning tool — isn't it?, Apostrophes: Keep straight and curly apostrophes), the [Remove Punctuation](/remove-punctuation) returns Cleaned text: Hello world It's a useful textcleaning tool isn't it, Characters removed: 5, Words remaining: 9, Line breaks preserved: 0. The first figure is the headline result, and the rest break it down so you can see how the total is made up. ## Cleaning is not always harmless normalisation

Punctuation can distinguish 3.14 from 314, an email address from its parts, or a hyphenated identifier from a joined string. This tool is appropriate when those distinctions are intentionally unnecessary. It should not be applied blindly to source code, structured data, passwords, web addresses or numeric values whose separators matter.

## Unicode letters and apostrophes

The expression retains letters and numbers across languages rather than restricting input to A–Z. Keeping apostrophes preserves common contractions such as it's and isn't. Other marks, including hyphens and typographic dashes, are removed without inserting replacement spaces, so hyphenated words can join together.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Replace punctuation with spaces first if you need to prevent words joining.
- Do not clean structured code, URLs or decimals with a general punctuation stripper.
- Keep a source copy so the transformation remains reversible.

## Frequently asked questions

### Does this preserve line breaks?

Yes. Spaces, tabs and newline characters are retained; only characters outside the allowed letter, number, whitespace and selected apostrophe categories are removed. Try it with your own numbers in the [Remove Punctuation](/remove-punctuation) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Will hyphenated words stay separate?

The hyphen is removed rather than replaced by a space, so a hyphenated pair becomes joined. Pre-process with a space if separation is required. Try it with your own numbers in the [Remove Punctuation](/remove-punctuation) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Does it work with accented or non-Latin text?

Yes. Unicode letter and number categories are preserved, rather than limiting the result to English ASCII characters. Try it with your own numbers in the [Remove Punctuation](/remove-punctuation) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What formula does the Remove Punctuation use?

Keep every character in Unicode letter, number or whitespace categories, plus apostrophes in keep mode. Remove all other punctuation and symbol characters without changing line structure. You can see it in action in the [Remove Punctuation](/remove-punctuation) — enter your own values and the result updates as you type.
